The main takeaway from our work is that

, in addition to the usual evaluation of absolute changes in the probability distribution of precipitation extremes, it is also useful to evaluate the fractional change in this probability distribution.

, in contrast to the widespread belief that climate models are unable to simulate precipitation extremes, most models are able to simulate the key features of extreme probability distributions in current climate and can thus be used with some confidence to evaluate future changes.

, for the two measures we have tested, the current range of uncertainty in the observational estimates is sufficiently large to mask model biases in simulating precipitation extremes, which suggests that the use of fractional changes in the probability is a reasonable approach to evaluate changes in the probability under climate change.
